variants.notes: Word-level editing (replace / insert / delete) of a recording: only the changed words are regenerated with OmniVoice masked-middle inference (audio context on both sides), the rest of the waveform is untouched sample for sample. Uses the released Amharic OmniVoice weights. Deletes = cut + 0.32 s seam regeneration. Several changes per call (right to left). Refuses: num_step < 16, audio > 30 s, orig_text that disagrees with the ASR transcript (CER > 0.6, unless force=True), no word change. cpu-int8 is borderline-slow (about 14-18 s per edit on 6 fast ARM cores; x86 not measured): offer it as opt-in only. Edited audio is synthetic: label it in the UI.

variants.entry: tts_small_infer.py: AmharicTTS(threads=4, int8=True).synth(text, voice=None|path) -> float32 numpy at 24 kHz
requires_python: pocket-tts (tested: git v4.0.1-19-gee2ebc8, github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts; the PyPI 4.0.1 wheel is untested)
variants.license: pocket-tts code: MIT. Base weights: Kyutai Pocket TTS, CC-BY-4.0 under Kyutai's gated acceptable-use policy (accepted). Fine-tune training data: Amilia (YouTube-derived Amharic speech), non-commercial use only. amharic-ctc was used only for data filtering, alignment and evaluation.
variants.notes: Kyutai Pocket TTS English 24-layer teacher fine-tuned on Amharic (new sentencepiece text embedding; 964 h news to step 5k, then 1,593 h news+podcasts to 15k, then 2.5k polish steps at lr 5e-5 on 415 h of the cleanest clips), distilled to 6 layers with classifier-free guidance (cfg 2.0) baked in, so inference is a single pass with no CFG. Voice cloning from a 3-5 s clip, no transcript needed. synth() generates sentence by sentence (split on ። ? !), 0.2 s pause between sentences. Digits and Latin script are read poorly: spell numbers out. int8 is not less intelligible than fp32 (app path, clean100: fp32 0.061 / int8 0.053). Slightly less accurate than OmniVoice (clean100 0.053 vs 0.047, speaker sim 0.956 vs 0.961) but runs about 2x faster than real time on 4 CPU cores, where OmniVoice int8 is 5-8x slower than real time.
